messages:
olivia: Noticed a drop in KMS audit events after the onprem hardening roll — roughly 20:03-20:07 UTC. Audit sink shows missed batches. Anyone aware of recent RBAC/netpol churn?
raj: We tightened infra netpols at 3850012000 (deny-all egress + explicit allows). Did the shipper run in hostNetwork or use node SNAT?
tom: Shipper is daemonset hostNetwork=false, relies on pod egress. If netpol default-deny hit, it would block reach to logging-proxy. What error do the shipper pods show?
olivia: Shipper logs: "failed to connect 10.40.2.7:443: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority" and then repeated buffer full warnings. We rotated the internal CA earlier this morning.
raj: Sounds like CA bundle mismatch + netpol preventing fallback to proxy. Two things: restore connectivity to allow immediate replay; and ensure future cert rotations don't create silent gaps.
tom: Quick fix: allow egress from infra namespace to 10.40.2.7/32 TCP 443 and patch the shipper secret with new CA. Command: `kubectl patch secret logging-ca -n infra -p '{"data":{"ca.crt":"<newbundlebase64>"}}'` then rollout restart daemonset/logging-shipper.
olivia: Applying allow and patching now. Also copying local archives from nodes /var/log/kms-audit/*.tar.gz before restart.
sec-bot: incident-note: potential audit gap 3850012000-3850012300. severity: medium. owners: @olivia @raj.
raj: Postmortem actions: 1) CI job to rotate CA and verify shipper trust update, 2) dual-write audit sink (object-store + SIEM), 3) netpol template that includes temporary auto-allow for logging during certroll, 4) RBAC: ensure shipper SA has secret:get for logging-ca secret and a scoped RoleBinding so controller changes can't remove it silently.
tom: I'll own the CI test. Olivia, can you draft the runbook steps for rehydration and customer notification if gap >5m?
olivia: On it. Will post runbook here for review.
